title: Canary Thermometer: lightweight canary prober plus eval-checksum suite for preflight gates
creator: Avery Chen
description: We are building a small-footprint canary prober (the 'Canary Thermometer') and an accompanying eval-checksum suite intended to run as a preflight gate for all runtime and model rollouts. Goals: (1) surface regressions quickly with <5 minute turnarounds for critical KPIs, (2) provide deterministic signal for functional regressions using checksumable evals, and (3) minimize cost and noise so it can run as part of daily automated verification and as part of staged canaries. The prober will execute three parallel lanes: fast-smoke (latency/availability), perf-sampler (short synthetic bursts to estimate token throughput and P50/P95), and checksum-evals (deterministic prompts with controlled randomness to detect output drift). Key trade-offs: using deterministic prompts increases signal precision for regression detection but may miss emergent data-dependent regressions; adding stochastic evals increases coverage but requires larger sample sizes and more compute. Implementation choices: lightweight containers with pinned model versions, sampling harness that replays a small set of in-production-like requests, KV cache warmup phase, and telemetry tags to correlate with rollout IDs and region. The prober emits compact KPIs and a signature checksum blob stored in our staging metadata service for regression diffs and triage. The system integrates with rollout orchestrator to mark canary status and optionally trigger automatic rollback when KPI thresholds are breached.
comments: 2026-01-18: Initial ticket created after spike; spec draft uploaded to Confluence and linked below.
2026-01-21: Design review with Runtime and Observability teams. Decided to keep checksum evals small (<=20 prompts) but deterministic; add a randomized-stochastic lane as optional background job.
2026-01-28: Prototype implemented for fast-smoke lane. Early runs show median latency regression detection within 3 runs for injected 10% tail latency increase.
2026-02-02: Perf-sampler added; discovered noisy P95 due to cold KV cache. Added a 60s cache-warmup step and an explicit 'simulate-warm' flag to remove false positives.
2026-02-07: Observability owner (Marco Alvarez) requested additional tags: rollout_id, canary_stage, model_variant, and quantization_profile. PR opened to add tags and trace spans.
2026-02-10: Integrated with rollout orchestrator to report a pass/fail boolean and detailed KPI payload. Still pending final runbook approval for auto-rollback policy.
acceptance_criteria: Canary Thermometer runs in <=5 minutes for the fast-smoke lane and <=15 minutes for full suite
Checksum-evals detect injected deterministic output changes (single-token substitution) with >95% confidence across CI runs
Perf-sampler stabilizes P50/P95 within ±10% across 5 consecutive runs after KV warmup
Run outputs are emitted to telemetry with rollout_id and stored in historical index for diffing
Integration test with rollout orchestrator causes canary to fail if any critical KPI threshold is exceeded and logs an incident ticket
risks: False positives from cold-start effects if KV warmup is insufficient
Checksum evasion for non-deterministic outputs when model sampling is enabled
Added runtime cost if suite runs too frequently — need throttles and budget-aware scheduling
Auto-rollback on noisy signals could cause unnecessary rollbacks without additional smoothing/aggregation
next_steps: Finalize runbook and auto-rollback policy with SRE and Product (due 2026-02-15)
Merge telemetry PR and verify Grafana dashboards show stable baselines
Add synthetic churn scenarios to acceptance harness to validate smoothing heuristics
Coordinate with Dedicated/Private teams to validate prober runs within isolated VPCs and with customer model variants
